learn.keyword: what is rsi in share market
learn.title: What Is RSI in Share Market? A Simple Guide | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: RSI explained in plain words: what the 0 to 100 number means, why 70 and 30 matter, and how to read it on a NEPSE stock like NABIL.
learn.lead: RSI is a number from 0 to 100 that shows how strong recent price moves have been.

paragraphs: RSI stands for Relative Strength Index. It compares the size of recent up days with the size of recent down days and turns that into a number between 0 and 100.
When a stock has mostly gone up lately, RSI is high. When it has mostly gone down, RSI is low. Most charts look back over the last 14 trading days, and so does StockYan.
Three lines matter most on an RSI chart: 30, 50 and 70. You will see them drawn as guides on most RSI charts.
points: Above 70: the price has risen fast. Traders call this overbought.
Below 30: the price has fallen fast. Traders call this oversold.
Around 50: up days and down days are roughly balanced.
Above 50 leans up. Below 50 leans down.

paragraphs: A high RSI only says the price rose quickly. Strong stocks can stay above 70 for weeks, and weak stocks can stay below 30 for a long time.
So many traders treat RSI as a prompt to look closer. A reading of 75 asks a question: is this rise backed by volume and good results, or are buyers running out?

Divergence is when price and RSI disagree. If the price makes a new high but RSI makes a lower high, the push upward is getting weaker. If the price makes a new low but RSI makes a higher low, the selling is getting weaker.
Divergence is rare and it can fail. Treat it as an early warning to watch the chart more closely.
In NEPSE, a bonus share book closure makes the price drop in one day even though nothing bad happened. The company simply split the same value across more shares.
An RSI worked out on raw prices sees that drop as heavy selling. StockYan works out RSI on prices adjusted for bonus and right shares, so the number reflects real buying and selling.

body.h2: How to use RSI on NEPSE
paragraphs: RSI is one tool among several. These habits help it make sense.
points: Read RSI with the price chart, never alone.
Check volume. A move on high volume means more.
Use support and resistance to see where price may pause.
Compare a stock's RSI with its own past readings.

paragraphs: Every stock page in StockYan shows its RSI. The RSI scanner lists all NEPSE stocks by RSI, shows which ones crossed 30 or 70 today, and flags divergence.
Nabil Bank (NABIL) closed at Rs 542 on 27 Oct 2026. Its 14-day RSI that day was 61.58, above the 50 midline, so recent up days outweighed down days.
A month earlier the reading was higher. On 24 Sep 2026 NABIL's RSI was 73.95, above 70. By 5 Oct it had fallen to 47.64. It then climbed back to 72.02 on 16 Oct before easing to 61.58.

On 30 Sep 2026, NABIL's book closure for a 5% bonus share took place. The raw price fell from Rs 566 to Rs 530.70 that day, which looks like a 6% drop. After adjusting for the bonus, the real move was a fall of about 1.5%.

faq.q: What is a good RSI value?
faq.a: There is no single good value. Many traders read above 70 as stretched up and below 30 as stretched down, then look at the trend and volume before doing anything.

faq.q: What RSI period should I use?
faq.a: 14 days is the standard and what most charts use. A shorter period reacts faster but gives more false moves.

faq.q: Where can I see RSI for all NEPSE stocks?

learn.title: MACD Indicator Explained for Beginners | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: What MACD is, what the MACD line, signal line and histogram mean, and how to read a crossover. With a real NABIL example from NEPSE.
learn.lead: MACD shows whether a stock's trend is speeding up or slowing down.

paragraphs: MACD stands for Moving Average Convergence Divergence. It compares two moving averages of the price: a fast one and a slow one. Most charts use 12 days for the fast one and 26 days for the slow one.

A moving average is the average closing price over a set number of days. When the fast average pulls further above the slow one, prices are rising faster than before. When it sinks toward or below the slow one, the rise is cooling.

body.h2: The parts of a MACD chart
paragraphs: A MACD chart sits under the price chart and has a few pieces.
points: MACD line: the fast average minus the slow average.
Signal line: a 9-day average of the MACD line.
Histogram: bars showing the gap between the two lines.
Zero line: where the two averages are equal.

paragraphs: When the MACD line crosses above the signal line, short-term momentum is turning up. When it crosses below, momentum is turning down.
Where the cross happens matters. A cross above the zero line happens inside an uptrend. A cross below the zero line happens inside a downtrend.
Tall bars mean the MACD line is far from the signal line, so momentum is strong. Shrinking bars mean the gap is closing, which often comes before a crossover.
Shrinking bars are a sign to watch. They do not always lead to a turn.
MACD is built from moving averages, so it reacts after the price has already moved. In a sideways market it can cross back and forth many times and give mixed readings.
It works best next to the price chart, support and resistance, and volume. Many traders also check RSI to see how stretched a move is.

Like RSI, MACD can disagree with the price. If the price makes a higher high while the MACD line makes a lower high, the upward push is weakening. If the price makes a lower low while MACD makes a higher low, selling is easing.
Divergence is an early warning. It can last a long time before the price turns, and sometimes the price does not turn at all.
When you open a MACD chart, ask four quick questions.
points: Is the MACD line above or below zero?
Is the histogram growing or shrinking?

paragraphs: On 27 Oct 2026, Nabil Bank (NABIL) closed at Rs 542. Its daily MACD line was 4.30 and its signal line was 3.71, so the histogram was 0.59.
Both lines were above zero, and the MACD line was above the signal line. That reads as an uptrend with momentum still positive.
The histogram was shrinking, though, which means the push was fading. That is something to keep an eye on in the next sessions.

faq.q: What are the usual MACD settings?
faq.a: Most charts use 12, 26 and 9: a 12-day and a 26-day average for the MACD line, and a 9-day average for the signal line.

faq.q: Is MACD better than RSI?
faq.a: They answer different questions. RSI shows how stretched a move is. MACD shows whether the trend is speeding up or slowing. Many traders look at both.

faq.q: How do I find MACD crossovers on NEPSE?
faq.a: Open the MACD scanner in StockYan to see stocks where the MACD line crossed the signal line.

learn.keyword: support and resistance in share market
learn.title: Support and Resistance in Share Market, Simply | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: Learn what support and resistance are, why prices pause at certain levels, and how to find them on a NEPSE chart. Real NABIL levels inside.
learn.lead: Support is a price where buyers tend to step in. Resistance is where sellers tend to show up.

paragraphs: Support is a price level where a falling stock has stopped and turned up before. Buyers saw the price as cheap there, so they bought and the fall paused.
The more times a price has bounced from the same level, the more people notice it and the more attention it gets next time.
Resistance is the opposite. It is a level where a rising stock has stalled before, because holders sold to take profit or to get out at break-even.
A common resistance is the 52-week high, the highest price of the past year. Many holders watch it.
Levels do not hold forever. When the price closes clearly above resistance on good volume, it is called a breakout. When it closes clearly below support, it is called a breakdown.
After a breakout, old resistance often becomes new support. Traders call this a role reversal.
Prices often react near round numbers, like Rs 500 or Rs 1,000, because many people place orders there. Old highs and lows from past months work the same way.
You can draw levels yourself with a few simple rules.
points: Look for prices where the chart turned several times.
Treat a level as a zone, a small range of prices.
Use daily closes and ignore one-off spikes.
More touches means more people are watching.

paragraphs: In NEPSE, bonus and right shares lower the share price at book closure. On a raw chart this leaves a gap that looks like a sharp fall, and levels drawn across that gap can be wrong.
StockYan can show prices adjusted for bonus and right shares, so old levels line up with today's price.

Levels help you think before you trade. Note the nearest support and resistance, then look at how far the price could move each way. If resistance is close and support is far below, the room to rise is small compared with the room to fall.
In NEPSE a stock can move at most 15% in a day, so a level far from the price can take several sessions to reach.
Here is StockYan's support and resistance ladder for Nabil Bank (NABIL) at the close on 27 Oct 2026, when it traded at Rs 542.
The nearest support was around Rs 532.43, about 1.8% below the price. The price had touched this zone 8 times between 10 Mar and 28 Sep 2026. A deeper support sat near Rs 509.29, with 10 touches.
The nearest resistance was the 52-week high of Rs 581, about 7.2% above the price. Between the two, the stock had room to move in either direction.

faq.q: What is support and resistance in simple words?
faq.a: Support is a price where a stock has stopped falling before. Resistance is a price where it has stopped rising before. Both are places where many buyers or sellers have acted in the past.

faq.q: How reliable are support and resistance levels?
faq.a: They often slow the price down, but any level can break, especially on news or results. Treat them as zones to watch.

faq.q: Can StockYan find these levels for me?
faq.a: Yes. The support and resistance scanner and the chart's levels tool mark the zones from real price touches.

learn.title: EMA vs SMA: Moving Averages Explained | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: What a moving average is, how EMA and SMA differ, and what a golden cross means. A simple guide with a real NABIL example from NEPSE.
learn.lead: A moving average smooths out daily price noise so the trend is easier to see.

paragraphs: A moving average is the average closing price over the last few days, worked out again every day. A 20-day average adds up the last 20 closes and divides by 20.
On a chart it becomes a smooth line that follows the price. When the price is above the line, the recent trend is up. When it is below, the trend is down.
SMA means Simple Moving Average. Every day in the window counts the same.
It is steady and easy to understand. The trade-off is that it is slow to react when the price suddenly changes direction.
EMA means Exponential Moving Average. It gives more weight to recent days, so it turns sooner when the price changes direction.
The cost is more false turns. A short EMA can flip back and forth when the market moves sideways.

Neither is better in every case. Short-term traders often prefer EMA because it reacts sooner. Longer-term investors often use SMA because it is calmer. The length you choose matters as much as the type.

In an uptrend, the price often dips back to a rising moving average and then moves on. Many traders watch the 20-day or 50-day average as a moving support line. In a downtrend, a falling average often acts as resistance.
When a faster average crosses above a slower one, it is called a golden cross. When it crosses below, it is called a death cross.
Crossovers come after the move has started, so they confirm a trend more than they predict one. In a sideways market they can give many false crosses.
A bonus book closure lowers the share price in one day. On raw prices, the moving average then sits far above the price for weeks and can show a false death cross.
StockYan's indicators use prices adjusted for bonus and right shares, which avoids this.
On 27 Oct 2026, Nabil Bank (NABIL) closed at Rs 542. Its 9-day EMA was Rs 540.76 and its 20-day EMA was Rs 536.93.
The price was above both lines, and the faster line was above the slower one. StockYan's EMA scanner had marked a golden cross between these two averages on 10 Sep 2026, 47 days earlier.
The gap between the two lines was small, about 0.7%. That points to a steady trend that was not racing ahead.

faq.q: What is the difference between EMA and SMA?
faq.a: SMA gives every day the same weight. EMA gives recent days more weight, so it reacts faster to new moves.

faq.q: Which moving average is best for NEPSE?
faq.a: There is no best setting. Many traders use 9 and 20-day EMAs for short swings and 50 and 200-day SMAs for the bigger trend. Pick lengths that match how long you hold.

faq.q: What is a golden cross?
faq.a: A golden cross is when a faster moving average crosses above a slower one. It shows the recent trend has turned up.

learn.title: Bollinger Bands Explained in Plain English | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: What Bollinger Bands are, what a squeeze means, and how to read price near the upper or lower band. Real NABIL numbers from 27 Oct 2026.
learn.lead: Bollinger Bands draw a channel around the price that widens when it moves a lot and narrows when it is quiet.

paragraphs: Bollinger Bands are three lines drawn on a price chart.

Standard deviation is a measure of how far prices usually stray from their average. When prices swing a lot, it grows and the bands move apart. When prices are calm, it shrinks and the bands move closer.
points: Middle band: the 20-day simple moving average.
Upper band: the middle band plus 2 standard deviations.
Lower band: the middle band minus 2 standard deviations.

paragraphs: Most closes land inside the bands. A close near the upper band means the price is high compared with its recent average. A close near the lower band means it is low.
Touching a band is not a signal by itself. In a strong uptrend, the price can ride along the upper band for many days.
When a stock closes near the upper band day after day, traders say it is walking the band. It is a sign of strength. Reading every touch of the upper band as a top would miss many strong runs.
When the bands get very close together, it is called a squeeze. It means the price has been unusually calm.
Calm periods often end with a bigger move, but a squeeze does not say which way. Traders wait for a close outside a band to see the direction.
Bollinger Bands show where price sits compared with its recent range. Other tools fill in the rest.
points: Pair them with RSI to see if a move is stretched.
Check volume when price closes outside a band.
Use support and resistance for nearby levels.

paragraphs: Two numbers sum up the bands. %B shows where the close sits: 0 is the lower band, 1 is the upper band and 0.5 is the middle.
Bandwidth is the distance between the upper and lower band as a share of the middle band. A low bandwidth means a squeeze.
These are the habits that most often lead beginners astray.
points: Treating every band touch as a turn.
Ignoring the trend the bands sit in.
Guessing which way a squeeze will break.

paragraphs: On 27 Oct 2026, Nabil Bank (NABIL) closed at Rs 542. Its 20-day Bollinger Bands were: upper Rs 548.44, middle Rs 537.06 and lower Rs 525.68.
The close sat above the middle band and below the upper band, about 72% of the way up the channel.
The bands were about 4.2% apart, so the price had been fairly calm. They were not tight enough for StockYan to flag a squeeze. In the numbers above, %B was 0.72 and bandwidth was 4.24%.

faq.q: What are the standard Bollinger Bands settings?
faq.a: 20 days for the middle band and 2 standard deviations for the outer bands. Most traders keep these, since they are what most charts show.

faq.q: What does a Bollinger Band squeeze mean?
faq.a: The bands have moved close together because the price has been calm. A bigger move often follows, but the squeeze does not show its direction.

faq.q: Can I scan NEPSE stocks by Bollinger Bands?
faq.a: Yes. StockYan's Bollinger scanner lists stocks in a squeeze or closing outside a band.

learn.title: Fibonacci Retracement Levels, Simply Explained | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: What Fibonacci retracement is, what 38.2%, 50% and 61.8% mean, and how traders draw it on a swing. With real NABIL levels from NEPSE.
learn.lead: Fibonacci retracement marks where a pullback inside a trend might pause.

paragraphs: Prices rarely move in a straight line. After a big rise, they often give back part of it before the next move. This is called a pullback or retracement.
Fibonacci retracement is a way to measure how far a pullback has gone. You pick a swing low and a swing high, and the tool draws lines at set percentages of that move.
The usual levels come from ratios in the Fibonacci number series, which is where the name comes from.
points: 61.8%: a deep pullback, linked to the golden ratio

paragraphs: Traders watch these lines as places where a pullback could stop. The area between 50% and 61.8% gets the most attention and is sometimes called the golden zone.
The levels have no special power. They work partly because many people watch them. They are most useful when they line up with an old support level or a moving average.
In a downtrend, draw from the swing high down to the swing low. The levels then mark how far a bounce might go before sellers return.
The result depends on which low and high you pick. Use clear turning points on the daily chart and skip small wiggles.
On NEPSE, use adjusted prices. A bonus book closure on a raw chart can create a fake swing low that throws every level off.

Fibonacci levels can also be drawn past the swing high, for example at 141.4% and 161.8% of the move. These are called extensions. Some traders use them as possible targets if a rise carries on past the old high.
Fibonacci is easy to draw and easy to misuse.
points: Picking a swing that is too small.
Drawing on raw prices across a bonus.
Expecting price to stop exactly on a line.

paragraphs: StockYan's Fibonacci scanner measured Nabil Bank's (NABIL) rise from a swing low of Rs 461.90 on 13 Jan 2026 to a swing high of Rs 553.33 on 15 Sep 2026. Both prices are adjusted for bonus shares.
That gave these retracement levels: 23.6% at Rs 531.75, 38.2% at Rs 518.40, 50% at Rs 507.62 and 61.8% at Rs 496.83.
On 27 Oct 2026 NABIL closed at Rs 542, above the 23.6% level. The pullback from the September high had been shallow so far.

faq.q: What is the golden zone in Fibonacci retracement?
faq.a: It is the area between the 50% and 61.8% levels. Many traders watch it as a place where a deeper pullback might stop.

faq.q: Does Fibonacci retracement work on NEPSE?
faq.a: It is a way of marking levels, so it can be drawn on any chart. Treat the levels as areas to watch, and check them against support, volume and the trend.

faq.q: Which Fibonacci levels matter most?
faq.a: 38.2%, 50% and 61.8% are the ones most traders watch.

learn.title: Candlestick Patterns for Beginners | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: How to read a candlestick, and what doji, hammer, engulfing and evening star patterns show. A simple guide with real NABIL candles.
learn.lead: One candle shows a full day of trading: where the price opened, where it closed and how far it moved.

paragraphs: Each candle covers one trading day. The thick part is the body. It runs from the opening price to the closing price.
A green body means the stock closed higher than it opened. A red body means it closed lower. The thin lines above and below the body are wicks. They show the day's high and low.
There are dozens of named patterns. Beginners only need a few to start.
points: Doji: open and close almost equal.
Hammer: small body, long lower wick, after a fall.
Shooting star: small body, long upper wick, after a rise.
Engulfing: one body fully covers the day before.
Evening star: three candles that can mark a top.

paragraphs: A bullish engulfing pattern is a green body that fully covers the red body of the day before. It shows buyers took over from sellers in one session. A bearish engulfing pattern is the reverse: a red body that covers the green body before it.

These are three-candle patterns. An evening star starts with a strong green candle, then a small candle, then a red candle that closes well into the first body. It can mark a top. A morning star is the mirror image after a fall.
A doji or a spinning top has a small body. The price moved during the day but ended close to where it started.
These candles show that buyers and sellers were evenly matched. They matter most after a long move, when they can show the move is tiring.
A pattern means little on its own. A hammer after a long fall, at a support level, on high volume, says much more than a hammer in the middle of a range.
Patterns also fail often. Many traders wait for the next candle to confirm, and use patterns together with levels and the trend.

NEPSE trades from Sunday to Thursday, 11:00 to 15:00, so each daily candle covers that four-hour session. A single stock can move at most 15% up or down in a day, which limits how tall one candle can get.
Here are the latest candles StockYan's candlestick scanner flagged for Nabil Bank (NABIL) in October 2026.
On 26 Oct, the price opened at Rs 547 and closed at Rs 543. The scanner marked an evening star, a pattern that can show a rise losing steam.

On 27 Oct, NABIL opened at Rs 543, went as high as Rs 545 and as low as Rs 540, and closed at Rs 542. The body was small with wicks on both sides, so the scanner marked a spinning top, a day of indecision.
Two cautious candles after a rise are worth watching. They do not decide what happens next.

faq.q: How many candlestick patterns should a beginner learn?
faq.a: Start with a handful: doji, hammer, shooting star, engulfing and morning or evening star. Learn these well before adding more.

faq.q: Do candlestick patterns work on NEPSE?
faq.a: They show how buyers and sellers behaved in a session, so the idea applies to any market. They are more useful at support or resistance and when volume is high.

faq.q: Can StockYan find candlestick patterns for me?
faq.a: Yes. The candlestick scanner checks every NEPSE stock and lists the patterns it finds.

learn.title: What Is Floorsheet in NEPSE? How to Read It | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: A floorsheet lists every NEPSE trade with buyer broker, seller broker, quantity and rate. Learn to read it, with a real NABIL example.
learn.h1: How to read a NEPSE floorsheet
learn.lead: The floorsheet is the full list of trades NEPSE recorded in a day.

paragraphs: Every time shares change hands on NEPSE, the exchange records the trade. The floorsheet is the list of all those trades for a day.
It is public, so anyone can see how many shares traded, at what price, and through which brokers.
Each row is one trade. These are the columns you will see.
You do not need to read every row. A few totals tell most of the story.
points: Pick the stock you care about.
Note the total shares and trades.
Add up shares by buying broker.
Add up shares by selling broker.
Compare with the past few weeks.

paragraphs: Because each row shows broker numbers, you can add up which brokers bought or sold the most of a stock. That is what broker analysis and accumulation tools do for you.
A broker trades for many clients, so a broker number does not reveal who the investor was.
NEPSE trades from Sunday to Thursday, 11:00 to 15:00. A day's floorsheet is complete once the session closes.
The floorsheet does not show why someone traded or what they will do next. Heavy buying through one broker can be one big investor or many small ones.
Use it next to the price chart, volume and the company's results.
StockYan shows the floorsheet for each stock and for the whole market, with buyer, seller, quantity, rate and amount. On desktop, filters and totals sit beside one large table.
On 27 Oct 2026, Nabil Bank (NABIL) traded 26,465 shares in 296 trades and closed at Rs 542.
Adding up that day's floorsheet by broker, broker number 75 bought the most: 6,189 shares, about 23% of all shares traded. On the selling side, broker 58 sold the most, 3,267 shares.
Broker 58 also bought 1,933 shares that day, which put it among the top buyers too. It is a reminder that one broker serves many clients on both sides.

The top five buying brokers bought 14,936 shares in total, while the top five sellers sold 10,592. One day of numbers like this is only a clue. It becomes more useful when the same pattern repeats over weeks.

faq.q: What is the floorsheet in NEPSE?
faq.a: It is the public list of every trade NEPSE recorded in a day, with the stock, buying broker, selling broker, quantity, rate and amount.

faq.q: Can I see who bought a share from the floorsheet?
faq.a: You can see the buying and selling broker numbers. The names of the investors are not public.

faq.q: Where can I see today's NEPSE floorsheet?
faq.a: Open Floor Sheet in StockYan to see the day's trades, free, on phone and desktop.

learn.title: Share Broker Commission in Nepal: Rates, Fees | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: NEPSE broker commission is tiered by trade amount, with a Rs 10 minimum. See every rate, the SEBON fee and DP charge, with a worked example.
learn.lead: Every NEPSE buy and sell pays broker commission and a SEBON fee. Sells also pay a DP charge.

paragraphs: Broker commission is a percentage of the trade amount, which is the number of shares times the price. The rate gets smaller as the amount gets bigger.
SEBON is the Securities Board of Nepal, the market regulator. It charges 0.015% of the trade amount on both buys and sells.
DP stands for Depository Participant, the bank or broker that keeps your demat account. When you sell, you pay a DP charge of Rs 25 for each stock you sell.
If you sell at a profit, there is also capital gains tax. For individuals it is 7.5% of the profit if you held the shares under a year, and 5% if you held them longer.
When you buy, fees are added to what you pay. When you sell, fees come out of what you receive. So your break-even price is a little above your buying price, even before any tax.
Because of the Rs 10 minimum and the flat Rs 25 DP charge, very small trades lose a bigger share to fees.
Selling one share of a Rs 542 stock pays Rs 10 in commission. That is almost 2% of the sale, before the DP charge.
Say you buy 100 shares of Nabil Bank (NABIL) at Rs 542, its closing price on 27 Oct 2026. The trade amount is Rs 54,200.
That falls in the 0.33% band, so commission is Rs 178.86. The SEBON fee at 0.015% is Rs 8.13. Your total cost is Rs 54,386.99, or about Rs 543.87 per share.

If you later sold the same 100 shares at Rs 542, you would pay the same Rs 178.86 commission and Rs 8.13 SEBON fee, plus the Rs 25 DP charge. You would receive Rs 53,988.01. Buying and selling at the same price would cost about Rs 399 in fees.
To cover all those fees, the 100 shares would need to sell at about Rs 546.01, around 0.74% above Rs 542, before any tax on the profit.

faq.q: What is the broker commission rate in Nepal?
faq.a: It is 0.36% for trades up to Rs 50,000, then 0.33%, 0.31% and 0.27% for larger bands, and 0.24% above Rs 1 crore.

faq.q: Is there a minimum broker commission?
faq.a: Yes. The minimum is Rs 10 per trade.

faq.q: How can I calculate commission quickly?
faq.a: Use the Buy and Sell tabs in StockYan's calculator. Enter units and price, and it shows commission, SEBON fee, DP charge and the total.

learn.title: Capital Gain Tax on Shares in Nepal, Explained | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: Individuals in Nepal pay 7.5% capital gains tax on share profit if held under a year, and 5% if held longer. See how to work it out.
learn.h1: Capital gains tax on NEPSE shares
learn.lead: When you sell shares at a profit, part of that profit goes to tax. How much depends on how long you held them.

paragraphs: For individual investors, capital gains tax (CGT) on listed shares has two rates. Institutions follow different rules, and this guide covers individuals only.
points: 7.5% of the profit if held under one year
5% of the profit if held one year or more

paragraphs: Profit is what you receive from the sale after selling costs, minus what you paid including buying costs.
Selling costs are broker commission, the 0.015% SEBON fee and the Rs 25 DP charge. Buying costs are broker commission and the SEBON fee.
The holding period starts on the day you bought the shares. Once a holding passes one year, selling it pays 5% instead of 7.5%.
StockYan's portfolio shows when a holding crosses one year, so you can see when the lower rate applies.
Tax is worked out from your buying cost. Keep the purchase price of your shares up to date in MeroShare so the profit and the tax come out right.
If a holding is close to one year old, the lower rate can make a real difference on a large profit. The price can also move a lot in that time, so tax is one thing to weigh among several.
If you sell at a loss, there is no capital gains tax on that sale. You still pay commission, the SEBON fee and the DP charge.

body.h2: Working it out step by step
paragraphs: Follow these steps for any sale.
points: Minus buying amount and buying costs
Profit times 7.5% or 5% is the tax

paragraphs: Say you bought 100 shares of Nabil Bank (NABIL) at Rs 485, the low of its 52-week range, and sold them at Rs 542, its close on 27 Oct 2026. To keep the sums simple, this leaves out the 5% bonus shares NABIL gave in 2026.
Buying: Rs 48,500 plus Rs 174.60 commission (0.36%) and Rs 7.27 SEBON fee comes to Rs 48,681.88.
Selling: Rs 54,200 minus Rs 178.86 commission (0.33%), Rs 8.13 SEBON fee and Rs 25 DP charge leaves Rs 53,988.01.
Profit before tax is Rs 5,306.13. Held under a year, tax at 7.5% is Rs 397.96. Held a year or more, tax at 5% is Rs 265.31, which is Rs 132.65 less.

faq.q: What is the capital gains tax on shares in Nepal?
faq.a: For individuals it is 7.5% of the profit if the shares were held under a year, and 5% if they were held a year or longer.

faq.q: Do I pay capital gains tax on a loss?
faq.a: No. Capital gains tax applies only to profit.

faq.q: How do I calculate capital gains tax on shares in Nepal?
faq.a: Take the sale amount minus selling costs, then subtract the buying amount and buying costs. Multiply that profit by 7.5% or 5%. StockYan's Sell calculator does this for you.

learn.keyword: what is wacc in share market
learn.title: What Is WACC in Share Market? NEPSE Guide | StockYan
learn.metaDescription: In NEPSE, WACC is your average buying price per share across all purchases. Learn what it means, why it matters for tax and how to work it out.
learn.lead: WACC is the average price you paid for each share of a stock, across all your buys.

paragraphs: WACC stands for Weighted Average Cost of Capital. In finance textbooks it means a company's cost of money. In the Nepal share market, people use it for something simpler: your average buying cost per share.
It is weighted because bigger purchases count more than smaller ones.
Add up what you paid for every purchase of one stock, then divide by the total number of shares.
points: Cost of each buy = units × price
Total cost = all buys added together

paragraphs: Your profit, and so your capital gains tax, is worked out from your cost. If the cost on record is wrong, the tax can be wrong too.
That is why MeroShare has a section to record where and at what price you bought your shares.
Some people add buying commission and the SEBON fee to their cost. This gives a slightly higher WACC that matches the money that really left their bank account.
When you sell some of your shares, the WACC of the shares you keep stays the same. Only buying more, or receiving bonus or right shares, changes it.
Buying more shares at a lower price brings your WACC down. This is called averaging down.
It lowers the price you need to break even. It also puts more of your money into the same stock, so think about how much one company should take up in your portfolio.
IPO shares cost the issue price you applied at. Bonus shares add to your share count without a market-price purchase, so they change your average.
The cost used for bonus shares follows tax rules, so check the figure on record in MeroShare.
Say you bought 100 shares of Nabil Bank (NABIL) at Rs 485, the low of its 52-week range, and later 100 more at Rs 542, its close on 27 Oct 2026.
Total cost before fees: Rs 48,500 + Rs 54,200 = Rs 1,02,700. Total shares: 200. WACC: Rs 1,02,700 ÷ 200 = Rs 513.50 per share.
If you include buying commission and the SEBON fee, the two buys cost Rs 1,03,068.87 in total, or Rs 515.34 per share.
With NABIL at Rs 542 and a WACC of Rs 513.50, each share shows a gain of Rs 28.50 before fees and tax.

faq.q: What is WACC in NEPSE?
faq.a: It is your average buying price per share of a stock, across all your purchases. Bigger purchases count more.

faq.q: How do I calculate WACC for my shares?
faq.a: Multiply units by price for each purchase, add them up, and divide by the total units. The Averaging tab in StockYan's calculator does this for you.

faq.q: Where can I see my average cost?
faq.a: StockYan's portfolio shows your average cost for every holding after you sync MeroShare or upload a TMS file.
